experiment.title: Pendulum that wandered off the wall
experiment.headline: Can't tell yet: out-of-plane motion
experiment.blurb: The bob drifts toward the camera. Ghostline says it can't tell, and what to change.
experiment.description: A swing that started with a push toward the camera.

scene.description: A nut on a string, swinging, but the bob also moves toward and away from the camera.

initial_hypotheses.name: Nonlinear pendulum
initial_hypotheses.mechanism: The exact pendulum with no losses: gravity pulling the bob back along a circle.
initial_hypotheses.observable_signature: The amplitude never shrinks. Swings that get steadily smaller, with a residual that grows like a damped oscillation, refute it.

initial_hypotheses.name: Nonlinear pendulum with viscous damping
initial_hypotheses.mechanism: The exact pendulum plus drag proportional to speed (air and pivot).
initial_hypotheses.observable_signature: The amplitude decays exponentially: every swing is the same fraction smaller than the one before. If γ fits to zero, damping is not needed.

initial_hypotheses.name: Small-angle oscillator
initial_hypotheses.mechanism: The textbook small-angle pendulum, where the restoring force is proportional to the angle and the period does not depend on the amplitude.
initial_hypotheses.observable_signature: The period is the same at every amplitude. At 50° a real pendulum is about 7% slower, so the phase drifts out of step within a few swings.

quality_issues.note: The bob's apparent size changes during the swing.

quality_flags.title: Possible out-of-plane motion
quality_flags.detail: The bob's mask area varies by 11% and rises and falls with the swing (|r| = 0.71). The bob is drifting toward and away from the camera.

quality_flags.detail: A low-order curve explains more than 30% of what every model leaves behind, which means missing physics (or geometry).

confidence_reasons: Major quality flag: possible out-of-plane motion.
Every model leaves a systematic pattern in its residuals.
The reviewer's challenge stands after two rounds, so the verdict is contested.
caveats: Treat g as unmeasured for this clip.
conclusion.narrative_md: The best fit is a damped pendulum with g = 9.77 ± 0.68 m/s², but I do **not trust it**. The damping it needs (γ = 0.22 1/s) is far larger than the pivot or air could give, and the video shows the bob moving toward and away from the camera. The fit is probably using damping to imitate a perspective effect.

cant_tell.reason: The bob does not stay in the plane of the sheet, so the pixel-to-meter scale changes during the swing, and no model here can account for that.
fixes: Hang the pendulum from two strings (a V) so it can only swing in one plane.
Film from further back and use the 2x lens, which reduces the perspective error.
Start the swing with a push along the wall, not toward the camera.

events.title: Scale and timing calibrated
events.body_md: The A4 sheet gives **1.67 mm per pixel** with 0.60% uncertainty. Plane offset 2 cm; camera moved 0.3 px over the clip.

events.title: Hypothesis P1: Nonlinear pendulum
events.body_md:
The exact pendulum with no losses: gravity pulling the bob back along a circle.

$$\ddot\theta=-\frac{g}{L_\mathrm{eff}}\sin\theta$$

**Refuted if:** The amplitude never shrinks. Swings that get steadily smaller, with a residual that grows like a damped oscillation, refute it.

events.title: Hypothesis P2: Nonlinear pendulum with viscous damping
events.body_md:
The exact pendulum plus drag proportional to speed (air and pivot).

$$\ddot\theta=-\frac{g}{L_\mathrm{eff}}\sin\theta-\gamma\,\dot\theta$$

**Refuted if:** The amplitude decays exponentially: every swing is the same fraction smaller than the one before. If γ fits to zero, damping is not needed.

events.title: Hypothesis P0: Small-angle oscillator
events.body_md:
The textbook small-angle pendulum, where the restoring force is proportional to the angle and the period does not depend on the amplitude.

$$\ddot\theta=-\frac{g}{L_\mathrm{eff}}\,\theta$$

**Refuted if:** The period is the same at every amplitude. At 50° a real pendulum is about 7% slower, so the phase drifts out of step within a few swings.

events.title: Prediction made before any fit: Nonlinear pendulum
events.body_md:
Before looking at a single fit, I expect **Nonlinear pendulum**. I will count it refuted if this happens: The amplitude never shrinks. Swings that get steadily smaller, with a residual that grows like a damped oscillation, refute it.

The harness scores every model on the last 35% of the motion, which I never see.

events.title: Fit P1: Nonlinear pendulum
events.body_md:
Fitted on the first 65% of the motion, then forecast the rest.

- θ₀: **0.5674** (0.535 to 0.6) rad
- ω₀: **0.05072** (-0.00808 to 0.11) rad/s
- g: **9.911** (9.59 to 10.2) m/s²

Training RMSE **0.0554 rad**. Held-out RMSE **0.101 rad** (0.0799 to 0.128). Lowest on 0 of 3 splits.

events.title: Fit P2: Nonlinear pendulum with viscous damping
events.body_md:
Fitted on the first 65% of the motion, then forecast the rest.

- θ₀: **0.6832** (0.644 to 0.723) rad
- ω₀: **-0.1788** (-0.284 to -0.0737) rad/s
- g: **9.817** (9.64 to 9.99) m/s²
- γ (damping): **0.2229** (0.158 to 0.288) 1/s

Training RMSE **0.0306 rad**. Held-out RMSE **0.0301 rad** (0.0219 to 0.0383). Lowest on 3 of 3 splits.

events.title: Fit P0: Small-angle oscillator
events.body_md:
Fitted on the first 65% of the motion, then forecast the rest.

- θ₀: **0.5683** (0.536 to 0.601) rad
- ω₀: **0.05214** (-0.00666 to 0.111) rad/s
- g: **9.517** (9.21 to 9.82) m/s²

Training RMSE **0.0554 rad**. Held-out RMSE **0.101 rad** (0.0797 to 0.128). Lowest on 0 of 3 splits.

events.title: Rejected P1: Nonlinear pendulum
events.body_md: Held-out RMSE 0.101 rad against 0.0301 rad for Nonlinear pendulum with viscous damping: 3.3× worse, and the intervals do not overlap (0.0799 to 0.128 rad).

events.body_md: Held-out RMSE 0.101 rad against 0.0301 rad for Nonlinear pendulum with viscous damping: 3.3× worse, and the intervals do not overlap (0.0797 to 0.128 rad).

events.title: Winner: Nonlinear pendulum with viscous damping
events.body_md: Nonlinear pendulum with viscous damping predicts the held-out frames better than every rival, by more than the uncertainty.
